standard_prerequisites.name: On an affine scheme D_QCoh is the derived category of modules and the functor identifies cohomology

standard_prerequisites.name: On affines m-pseudo-coherence of an object agrees with m-pseudo-coherence of its module complex
A coherent sheaf on an affine Noetherian scheme is a finite module and conversely
For a complex of modules over a Noetherian ring m-pseudo-coherence is equivalent to coherent cohomology in degrees at least m and vanishing above

core_obligations: Reduction to affines: since X is quasi-compact, in both (1) and (2) the object E is bounded above, so the question is local on X; assume X = Spec(A) with A Noetherian (proof lines 2493-2495).

Transport: E corresponds to a complex of A-modules M by the affine comparison; m-pseudo-coherence of E agrees with that of M by the affine pseudo-coherence lemma; coherence of H^i(E) agrees with H^i(M) being a finite A-module by the properties lemma (proof lines 2496-2502).
Conclusion: the module-level Noetherian pseudo-coherence lemma gives the equivalence of (1) and (2), and the particular case follows by taking m unbounded (proof lines 2503-2504).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the affine Noetherian case using boundedness above and locality (proof lines 2493-2495).
Translate both conditions into module statements on Spec(A) (proof lines 2496-2502).
Apply the Noetherian module-level equivalence and read off the particular case (proof lines 2503-2504).
